reason: I rank scratch_lifetime first: it changes only stack reservation around the existing pack and consumers, so its correctness risk is lower than changes to operand layout or ZA use, though any speed effect is unknown. For k_loop_schedule, use the proposed W-register counter in both K loops; this differs from the measured loop schedules, but may compile identically and has modest upside. b_panel_layout and transpose_fusion have larger potential to change operand access, but add substantial packing or register-mapping risk; neither has measured support. za_four_tile_reuse changes FMOPA issue order without reducing K-loop work, and carries rounding risk under the fixed tolerance. panel_packing and cache_blocking describe the same N=64 helper experiment; rank both last because that helper is unavailable and requires host preparation and validation. No supplied measurement establishes a gain for any candidate, and the historical noisy scores do not identify a cause.
